title: A Ledger for the Harbor
premise: In 1914, Freya Crane drives for the suffragist Edith Marlowe and quietly reads the letters he carries, keeping a private ledger of names, debts, and promises in a harbor town that runs on shipping and secrets. When war comes, the army requisitions the town, its warehouses, and every record — including Freya's ledger — and the German-born dockworkers who built the harbor are declared enemies overnight. Among them is Anton Weiss, the shipwright to whom Freya once promised passage and protection in peacetime. Freya must steal back his own ledger from military custody, forge a network out of suffragists, smugglers, and clerks, and move Anton and his daughter north before the river ice breaks and the last boat leaves. He succeeds at terrible cost: the ledger burns, Edith is arrested, and Freya learns that identity is not what the state writes down but what one chooses to carry.
about_author: Paloma Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing requisition records from coastal towns on the North Atlantic. She writes historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Freya Crane delivers letters for suffragist Edith Marlowe, reading each before sealing it, and records debts and favors in his leather ledger. POV Freya. Establishes his habit of measuring the world by what fits in two hands; ends with the news of war reaching the harbor.

chapters.title: The Shipwright's Handshake
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: three years earlier, Freya promised Anton Weiss, a German-born shipwright, safe passage if ever things turned sour. POV Freya. Warm, uneasy beat — a promise made lightly in peacetime that now weighs like ballast.

chapters.title: Edith's Platform
chapters.summary: Edith speaks at a suffrage rally as rumors of requisition orders circulate. POV Edith. She notices the crowd thinning as patriotism swallows reform; emotional beat: fury braided with resolve.

chapters.title: The Harbor Lists Its Names
chapters.summary: Army officers arrive with forms; every resident of enemy birth must register. POV Freya. He watches neighbors become categories on paper and adds their real names to his ledger — an act of quiet defiance.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Soldiers seize the warehouses, the customs house, and all municipal records. POV Freya. The ledger itself is confiscated in the sweep; Freya realizes his own handwriting could hang half the town.

chapters.title: Anton Refuses the Train
chapters.summary: Anton is ordered to an internment camp inland but delays, hiding in the shipyard loft with his daughter Greta. POV Anton. Fear and stubborn pride; he will not leave while his boats sit unfinished.

chapters.title: A Clerk Named Hobbes
chapters.summary: Freya cultivates Corporal Hobbes, a bored records clerk, trading cigarettes for glimpses of the requisition inventory. POV Freya. The beat: shame at currying favor with an occupier, sharpening into purpose when he spots his ledger listed.

chapters.title: Greta Counts the Days
chapters.summary: Greta, twelve, keeps her own tally of soldiers, gulls, and days since school closed. POV Greta. Child's-eye terror rendered as arithmetic; she asks her father whether their name is a bad word now.

chapters.title: The Ice Begins to Talk
chapters.summary: Early winter; the river groans. Edith warns Freya that once ice breaks, river traffic resumes under naval control and escape becomes impossible until next winter. POV Edith. A ticking clock is set: weeks, not months.

chapters.title: Reading the Enemy's Mail
chapters.summary: Freya is conscripted to sort intercepted correspondence for the army — his literacy makes him useful to the very machine hunting his friends. POV Freya. Moral vertigo; he begins copying names out of the army's own files.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Box Forty-One
chapters.summary: Hobbes confirms the ledger sits in Box 41 of the requisitioned customs vault. POV Freya. Hope arrives hand-in-hand with dread: stealing it is treason, punishable by firing squad.

chapters.title: Edith's Arrest Warrant
chapters.summary: Authorities open a file on Edith for 'seditious association' after her rally. POV Edith. She refuses to flee, arguing the movement dies if its voices scatter; Freya begs her to reconsider.

chapters.title: Smugglers' Sunday
chapters.summary: Freya approaches the Vane brothers, harbor smugglers whose boats know the reeds better than the charts. POV Freya. Hard bargaining: they'll carry passengers north for a price he cannot yet pay.

chapters.title: What Greta Saw
chapters.summary: Greta witnesses a neighbor dragged from his shop and stops speaking. POV Greta. Silence as wound; Anton carries her past the burned bakery where the town's tolerance visibly ended.

chapters.title: Box Forty-One, First Attempt
chapters.summary: Freya volunteers for night filing duty and reaches the vault, but a new lock and a drunk sentry turn him back. POV Freya. Failure beat; he leaves a fingerprint on the dust and lies awake imagining it found.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: The Vanes name their price: the coordinates of a navy fuel cache Freya has seen in intercepted mail. POV Freya. Betrayal of one duty to honor another; he copies the coordinates and hates himself cleanly.

chapters.title: Edith Taken
chapters.summary: Edith is arrested mid-speech and held without charge. POV Edith, then Freya. Her composure cracks only when they confiscate her correspondence — including letters Freya never delivered.

chapters.title: Letters Never Delivered
chapters.summary: Freya breaks into the evidence room to retrieve Edith's seized letters, discovering among them his own undelivered confession of love to a woman who left years ago. POV Freya. Raw exposure; his secrets are no longer his alone.

chapters.title: Hobbes Looks Away
chapters.summary: Hobbes, disillusioned by a deportation he witnessed, hints he can lose Box 41's key for exactly one hour. POV Hobbes. The occupier grows a conscience; trust extended across enemy lines.

chapters.title: One Hour
chapters.summary: Freya steals the ledger from the vault, but finds pages already copied by intelligence officers — his network is half-known. POV Freya. Victory soured; the ledger is now both shield and indictment.

chapters.title: The Copied Pages
chapters.summary: Intelligence Captain Rourke interviews Freya casually, testing him against the copied names. POV Freya. Cat-and-mouse tension; Freya lies with a steady voice and sweats through his coat.

chapters.title: Anton's Last Boat
chapters.summary: Anton secretly finishes a small ketch in the loft, working by candle stub. POV Anton. Craft as prayer; each plank laid is a refusal to be made small.

chapters.title: Greta Speaks Again
chapters.summary: Greta breaks her silence to warn Freya that soldiers searched the shipyard. POV Greta. Her first words in weeks are someone else's name — the found family taking root.

chapters.title: Rourke Closes In
chapters.summary: Rourke arrests the Vane brothers on smuggling charges unrelated to Freya, but their ledgers mention 'the reader.' POV Rourke. The net tightens; Freya has perhaps four days.

chapters.title: Burning the Coordinates
chapters.summary: Freya destroys every paper connecting him to the Vanes, including pages torn from his own recovered ledger. POV Freya. Amputation as survival; grief for the version of himself who kept everything.

chapters.title: Visiting Edith
chapters.summary: Freya visits Edith under pretext of legal errands; she tells him to save Anton and let her case play out publicly. POV Edith. She reframes sacrifice as strategy; Freya refuses to accept it gracefully.

chapters.title: The Ice Cracks Early
chapters.summary: A warm front splits the river ice ahead of schedule; the navy moves patrol boats upriver within hours. POV Freya. The clock collapses from days to one night.

chapters.title: Loading at Moonset
chapters.summary: Freya, Anton, and Greta load the ketch with food, tools, and the ledger wrapped in oilcloth. POV Anton. Taut, procedural suspense; every sound is a verdict.

chapters.title: Sentry at the Slip
chapters.summary: A young sentry catches them at the waterline; Hobbes appears and claims he's already inspected the boat. POV Hobbes. The clerk spends his career to buy an hour; he walks Freya past the checkpoint himself.

chapters.title: Downriver in the Dark
chapters.summary: The ketch slips downriver between patrol lights; Greta steers while Anton repairs a fouled line under fire from a nervous picket. POV Greta. Terror transfigured into competence; the child saves them.

chapters.title: Rourke at the Empty Loft
chapters.summary: Rourke searches the shipyard, finds candle stubs and wood shavings, and understands — too late — who the reader was. POV Rourke. The hunter's cold fury; he issues warrants naming Freya Crane.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Open water, then neutral shores; Anton and Greta disembark at a fishing village where a cousin waits. POV Anton. Farewell without ceremony; the promise kept is quieter than the promise made.

chapters.title: What Freya Kept
chapters.summary: Freya turns back alone, choosing arrest over exile because Edith's trial needs a witness who can read the evidence. POV Freya. The inversion: the man who measured what can be carried chooses to carry nothing but testimony.

chapters.title: The Trial of Edith Marlowe
chapters.summary: Freya testifies, producing the ledger's surviving pages proving the 'sedition' was charity. POV Freya. Climax of conscience; the courtroom becomes the rally Edith never got to finish.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Edith is convicted but spared prison by public outcry; Freya is sentenced to labor at the very docks he grew up on. POV Edith. Bittersweet justice; power concedes the minimum and calls it mercy.

chapters.title: Docks Under Guard
chapters.summary: Freya serves his sentence loading ships beside men he once ferried secrets to; none acknowledge him, all protect him. POV Freya. Found family expressed in silence and shared bread.

chapters.title: Letter from the North
chapters.summary: A letter arrives via the Vanes' old routes: Anton's new yard, Greta in school, a hull named Edith Marlowe. POV Freya. Joy arriving as contraband; the promise ripened into a life.

chapters.title: The Ledger Burns
chapters.summary: On release, Freya burns the remaining ledger page by page, keeping only blank paper. POV Freya. Ritual of release; identity surrendered to memory rather than record.

chapters.title: Ice Breaks Again
chapters.summary: Spring, one year on: the river opens, the first free boat sails, and Edith — released, diminished, unbowed — stands beside Freya on the quay. POV Edith. Renewal without erasure; the town remembers imperfectly but remembers.

chapters.title: A Blank Page
chapters.summary: Freya takes work driving again, for whoever needs letters carried, and writes a single name on the ledger's first fresh page: his own. POV Freya. Resolution: he was never what the lists said; he is what he chose to carry.
